paragraphs: The comparison is based on the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 53-7061.00 page, the adjacent-occupation notes registered by this evidence route, and public occupational material for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial arrangement and does not constitute a conclusion about practice scope or interchangeable qualifications.

Dishwashers clean dishes and cookware and operate dishwashing machines; this occupation cleans vehicles, machinery and equipment and performs inspection and basic preparation, so the objects and the work environment differ.

People willing to repeat cleaning to a process at a fixed station suit the dishwashing direction; people willing to operate equipment outdoors and in a workshop to clean vehicles and machinery suit this occupation.
Mainly the cleaned dishes and cookware and dishwashing machine running records.
Dishwashers

Electric motor and power tool and related repairers diagnose and fix functional faults in electric motors and power tools; this occupation only cleans, inspects, lubricates and makes minor adjustments, and faults beyond its authority must be referred to maintenance.
People willing to do fault diagnosis and dismantling and repair suit that direction; people willing to apply cleaning standards and safe handling suit this occupation.
Mainly repair work orders and troubleshooting and acceptance records.
Electric motor and power tool and related repairers

Control valve and valve installers and repairers (except mechanical door) install and repair pipeline valves and control systems; this occupation only turns valves to procedure and adjusts the pressure and flow of cleaning equipment, and does not carry responsibility for valve installation and repair.
People willing to install and commission valves and control systems suit that direction; people willing to operate to procedure and record parameters suit this occupation.
Mainly valve installation and repair and commissioning reports.
Control valve and valve installers and repairers (except mechanical door)

Laundry and dry-cleaning workers clean linen and clothing and operate washing and dry-cleaning equipment; this occupation cleans vehicles, machinery and equipment, so the objects, materials and cleaning media differ.
People willing to clean and finish linen and clothing suit that direction; people willing to clean and prepare equipment and vehicles suit this occupation.
Mainly records of cleaning and finishing and handover of linen and clothing.
Laundry and dry-cleaning workers

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually means adding new skills and qualifications: the dishwashing and janitorial directions need deeper hygiene and chemical cleaning knowledge, the septic tank and sewer direction needs confined-space and sewage-work qualifications, the repair direction needs electrical and mechanical diagnostic training, the valve direction needs installation, commissioning and process knowledge, and the laundry and dry-cleaning direction needs fabric and washing-process knowledge. Cleaning, inspection and safety-record skills transfer, but each direction's authority and qualification system must be obtained afresh.

entries: Fit signal: you are willing to repeat the same set of steps well to the cleaning standard, rather than changing your approach by feel each time.
Fit signal: you wear protective equipment as required and keep working to procedure in wet and noisy conditions with chemical exposure.

paragraphs: The complete O*NET work styles list has 14 items, with dependability 63 and attention to detail 59 leading, and caution 29 and integrity 26; it is not only the dependability item. The editorial self-check covers working to procedure, checking and reporting habits, and the scores are not an individual threshold or a probability of a safety incident.

entries: Fit signal: you are in the habit of writing down parameter settings and inspection results so that others can take over and review.
Fit signal: you can accept a working pattern in which 89% are exposed to contaminants every day and 95% are in an enclosed vehicle or operate enclosed equipment every day.

paragraphs: Worth noting: putting finishing first ahead of following procedure shows up as a problem during equipment damage and safety inspections.

Interest orientation: the interest code for this occupation's content is RC (Realistic, Conventional), and daily tasks are mainly cleaning work and equipment operation, mixing cleaning solutions and managing consumables, and inspection and preparation and recording.

entries: Fit signal: if you enjoy the process of restoring dirty equipment to clean and finding damage in the check, this work will give you a sense of achievement.
Fit signal: if you pay more attention to standards and safety details, chemicals and equipment operation are equally a direction you can keep improving in over the long term.

paragraphs: This page does not screen posts by MBTI; no valid evidence of type-based hiring in this occupation was obtained, and it is not asserted that no employer uses it.

entries: Fit signal: you are willing to test whether you fit by first producing a job plan for a team leader to review, rather than starting and seeing what happens.
Fit signal: when a protection gap or a wrong parameter setting is pointed out, you correct it on your own initiative and build a checking habit.

paragraphs: Worth noting: Enneagram interpretations easily slide into personality diagnosis, and this page does not use it to judge fit.

The complete O*NET table has basic skills 10, transferable skills 25, knowledge 33 and abilities 52; monitoring 44, speaking 41, listening 38, and operations control/quality analysis 50; customer service 64, English 58, transportation 54, mathematics 37 and chemistry 35; near vision 66 and flexibility/manual dexterity 56. The excerpt does not mean there are no other skills or knowledge, and the scores are not an individual threshold.

entries: Fit signal: you can judge from the equipment manual which parameters may be adjusted and which parts must not be hosed down.
Fit signal: you are willing to use checklists and recording tools to manage consumables and jobs, leaving your attention for inspection and safety.

paragraphs: Worth noting: setting parameters from experience or skipping protection over the long term shows up as a problem during equipment damage and safety inspections; fixing the parameter ranges and protection requirements is the sustainable approach.

This occupation centres on on-site work, equipment operation and crew collaboration: the O*NET Work Context fields show 43% are in contact with others constantly, 43% consider working with a work group or team extremely important, and 45% have high responsibility for the health and safety of others.

entries: Fit signal: you can still complete protection and inspection to procedure under handover deadline pressure, rather than rushing the volume first.
Fit signal: you are willing to record and report damage or anomalies faithfully after finding them, even when it affects the shift's progress.

paragraphs: Worth noting: hiding damage or anomalies to avoid trouble turns personal risk into risk for the organisation and the next shift.
Dishwashers
Suitable signal: you are willing to repeat cleaning to a process at a fixed station and accept a high pace of cleaning volume.
Caution signal: that direction centres on food-contact hygiene for dishes and cookware, and its objects differ from the vehicles and equipment of this occupation.
Electric motor and power tool and related repairers
Suitable signal: you are willing to diagnose faults and dismantle and repair, and to carry responsibility for repair quality.
Caution signal: that direction requires electrical and mechanical diagnostic training, which differs from the cleaning and inspection of this occupation.
Control valve and valve installers and repairers (except mechanical door)
Suitable signal: you are willing to install and commission pipeline valves and control systems and to read process requirements.
Caution signal: that direction requires process and installation and commissioning knowledge, whereas operating parameters is only a small part of this occupation.
Laundry and dry-cleaning workers
Suitable signal: you are willing to clean and finish linen and clothing and to master washing processes and equipment.
Caution signal: the objects in that direction are fabrics rather than vehicles and machinery and equipment, and the media and processes differ considerably.

People willing to repeat work to cleaning standards, able to wear protection strictly and handle chemicals and equipment anomalies as required, and willing to record parameters and inspection results faithfully.
People unwilling to wear protection to procedure, inclined to skip checks or hide damage and anomalies under schedule pressure, or unable to accept a wet, noisy environment with chemical exposure.
